newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sabena 1996 passenger traffic up 3.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sabena 1996 passenger traffic up 3.2 pct.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena said on Thursday that its passenger traffic rose by 3.2 percent in 1996 to a record 5,163,077.

Sabena attributed the rise entirely to traffic growth -- in line with the market average - in the second half of the year. The first six months were steady compared with the year-earlier period, it said in a statement.
It said it transported an average 14,145 passengers per day.
Intercontinental traffic rose 5.2 percent due to Sabena's partnerships with Swissair, Austrian Airlines and Delta Air.
This enabled it to add a second daily flight to New York and commercialise 10 additional destinations in the United States in 1996.

Its European network carried 3.2 percent more passengers in 1996, compared with a rise of 18.7 percent in 1995. The two links with Asia -- Tokyo and Macao -- remained steady but the African network jumped 7.8 percent.
Sabena is 49.5 percent owned by Swissair.
